UPSTREAM: tools/power turbostat: show IRQs per CPU The new IRQ column shows how many interrupts have occurred on each CPU during the measurement inteval. This information comes from the difference between /proc/interrupts shapshots made before and after the measurement interval. The first row, the system summary, shows the sum of the IRQS for all CPUs during that interval. UPSTREAM: tools/power turbostat: detect and work around syscall jitter The accuracy of Bzy_Mhz and Busy% depend on reading the TSC, APERF, and MPERF close together in time. When there is a very short measurement interval, or a large system is profoundly idle, the changes in APERF and MPERF may be very small. They can be small enough that an expensive interrupt between reading APERF and MPERF can cause the APERF/MPERF ratio to become inaccurate, resulting in invalid calculation and display of Bzy_MHz. A dummy APERF read of APERF makes this problem much more rare. Apparently this 1st systemn call after exiting a long stretch of idle is when we typically see expensive timer interrupts that cause large jitter. For the cases that dummy APERF read fails to prevent, we compare the latency of the APERF and MPERF reads. If they differ by more than 2x, we re-issue them. Signed-off-by: Len Brown <len.brown@intel.com> (cherry picked from commit 0102b06747c7d24e334d2b27c4b43eed693676f1) Signed-off-by: Azhar Shaikh <azhar.shaikh@intel.com> BUG=chrome-os-partner:62334 TEST=run turbostat --debug. Note that this detection is not fool-proof, as the counter could reset several times and still result in new > old. Signed-off-by: Len Brown <len.brown@intel.com> Signed-off-by: Rafael J. elan_i2c: Try to use pid in fw name, with fallback Previously the elan_i2c driver was modified to append a product_id to the end of the filename of the firmware it requests during a firmware update. This caused issues when this version of the driver was used on old systems that had the old no-pid-appended filenames for their firmwares. In an attempt to fix this issue for old systems, the pid was removed from the filename entirely when the driver requests a firmware. Unfortunately, this just breaks firmware updating for any systems with the new with-pid-appended filenames for their firmwares. In this CL we implement the same two-tiered naming convention present in other versions of the elan*_i2c drivers in ChromeOS. First we query to see if there is a valid firmware with a pid appended to the filename. If there is, we use that. However if that file doesn't exist, this patch makes it so the driver will try a fallback filename that does not include the pid. This should work for all systems. BUG=chrome-os-partner:62529 TEST=built kernel and deployed on a kip (new-with-pid-appended) filenames and everything works great. When I manually modify the image to look like an old no-pid-appended system it still works. trunks: mask signals handled by the service in all threads The service object started by trunksd installs its own signal handlers to perform graceful shutdown. Before this change, the background thread was started with an empty signal mask, which resulted in the process killed before it could finish the graceful shutdown on the service thread. This change masks the signal handled by the service before starting the background thread. The thread then inherits the signal mask. BUG=chromium:687018 BUG=chromium:687022 TEST=with a running trunksd, run "kill `pidof trunksd`", check that shutdown messages are present in the log.
